newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine PM urges govt, parlt to pass 97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine PM urges govt, parlt to pass 97 budget.

text.p: Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko on Tuesday asked his government and parliament to complete work on the 1997 budget and said ministers' jobs could be on the line unless they forced the budget through.

"If we go the first half year without a budget and foreign credits, that time will have gone to waste," Lazarenko told the largely conservative parliament, which has been adamantly opposed to some tough measures outlined in the budget.

Speaking to deputies and ministers in parliament, he added: "I am assessing the situation realistically. I do not exclude that if the budget is not passed then significant changes in the government are possible -- including sacking the cabinet."
But Lazarenko, who said the budget had to be approved by the end of the month, also said a change in government at this time would hurt a country already "in crisis".
President Leonid Kuchma is the only person who can sack the government but if Lazarenko resigned or was dismissed the whole cabinet would have to be re-appointed.

Lazarenko was speaking a day after Kuchma accepted the resignation of leading reformist Viktor Pynzenyk, who quit in anger over budget delays and said the government showed no political will to push it through.

The budget, and a package of tax reforms underpinning it, would help clear the way for Ukraine to receive a $2.5 to $3 billion loan from the International Monetary Fund. But the government has not yet passed a revised budget to parliament.
"If the budget process is extended yet another couple of months then we will lose control of the situation in the country," Lazarenko said.
The budget and the package of nine tax laws -- parliament has approved just one so far -- were created by Pynzenyk and designed to pull Ukraine out of economic crisis.
Lazarenko said the budget would enable Ukraine to receive foreign credits. "We know we cannot balance the budget without this money," he said.
Some IMF money would be used to cover this year's projected budget deficit of 5.8 billion hryvnias, or four percent of gross domestic product using Western calculations.
Lazarenko set out a two-week schedule to review the eight outstanding tax laws, which would broaden the tax base and cut many Soviet-era benefits.
Lazarenko said the lack of foreign credits meant the government was using money intended to pay off its mounting 5.8 billion hryvnia wage debt to pay gas debts.

"By the first half of this year we should have cut the wage debt by 1.2 billion hryvnias, but instead we have sent these resources to Russia and Turkmenistan to pay off debts from 1993 to 1995," he said.
The tax laws also attempt to legalise the large shadow economy, estimated to make up 60 percent of economic activity.
